A quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other at right angles. It must be a…
questions.explain: Perpendicular bisecting diagonals: a rhombus (a square is a special case).

questions.prompt: Joining the midpoints of the sides of ANY quadrilateral always gives a…
questions.explain: Varignon’s theorem, from the midpoint theorem.

questions.prompt: In △ABC, a line through the midpoint of AB parallel to BC meets AC at P. What can you say about P?
options: P is the midpoint of AC
questions.explain: The converse of the midpoint theorem.

questions.prompt: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
questions.explain: That is the definition of a trapezium.

questions.prompt: Explain why the midpoints of any quadrilateral ABCD form a parallelogram PQRS.
questions.modelAnswer: Draw diagonal AC. In △ABC, P and Q are midpoints of AB and BC, so PQ ∥ AC and PQ = ½AC (midpoint theorem). In △ADC, S and R are midpoints of AD and DC, so SR ∥ AC and SR = ½AC. So PQ and SR are parallel and equal, which makes PQRS a parallelogram.
